title: Shen Kuo describes the magnetic compass needle (Dream Pool Essays)
summary: In his book Dream Pool Essays, dated 1088, the Song dynasty polymath Shen Kuo wrote about the magnetic compass needle. He reported that a needle rubbed with lodestone points south, though some point north, and discussed the compass's deflection from due south. One account calls his work a major breakthrough for navigation that came long before similar ideas reached Europe.

uncertainty.note: Sources date the book to 1088; Shen Kuo first visited his Dream Brook property in 1086.

as_recorded.value: One of Shen's biggest discoveries was the magnetic compass needle, which he wrote about in his book 'Dream Pool Essays' in 1088.

famous 11th-century book, Meng Xi Bi Tan ( Meng Ch’i Pi T’an or “Brush Talk from a Dream Book”; more commonly known as the “Dream Pool Essays”). In these pages he presents his theories on a variety of topics, including the deflection of the compass from due south: When the point of a needle is rubbed with the lodestone, then the sharp end always points south

where.modern_name: Zhenjiang, Jiangsu, China (near his Dream Brook property)

importance.justification: An early and influential written account of the magnetic compass needle, later important to navigation.
